subject: Order Form redlines: payment triggers, min-commit schedule, and tax responsibility
messages:
From: procurement@acmecorp.com
To: monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: jane.doe@acmecorp.com, legal@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-10-19T07:31:00-07:00
Subject: Draft order form for signature — payment triggers and tax allocation

Hi Monica,

Thanks for sending the updated order form (attached). Our procurement and legal teams reviewed and we have a handful of open items before we can route for signature:

1) Payment trigger — the current commercial table suggests invoices triggered on monthly usage with proration for mid-period changes. We need explicit language around: when a payment is triggered after a commit change (up or down), and whether Redwood will issue a prorated credit or invoice.

2) Minimum commit schedule — the spreadsheet shows a staircase (Q1 40%, Q2 30%, Q3 30%). We need confirmation that the sequence is firm and whether there are clawback or true-up mechanics on underutilization.

3) Net terms — our AP team typically requires Net45. The order form states Net30. Any flexibility here?

4) Taxes/withholding — Acme will not accept being contractually liable for withholdings in jurisdictions where local law would impose customer withholding; we need Redwood to clarify tax evidence requirements and whether Redwood will accept tax residency certificates to avoid withholding.

Attached: ACME_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf and our procurement checklist. Can you run this by your legal/finance and confirm proposed redline language or countertext? We are aiming to finalize by EOD Thu so we can include this in our quarter close.

Thanks,
Procurement Team
Acme Analytics

-----

From: monica.patel@redwood.com
To: procurement@acmecorp.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft order form for signature — payment triggers and tax allocation

Thanks — appreciate the quick review and the clear bullets. High-level responses below and next steps:

- Payment trigger/proration: Redwood is comfortable committing to explicit proration for mid-period upsells. For downsells we propose a 30-day notice window before a reduced commit takes effect and a one-time true-up invoice for prior underutilization rather than retroactive credits. I’ll circulate specific contract language for the order form that matches this flow.

- Minimum commit schedule: The staircase as proposed is acceptable from a commercial standpoint; we will add an explicit clause describing true-up and clawback thresholds (e.g., if usage < 70% of committed in a quarter, schedule an automatic true-up invoice for the shortfall).

- Net terms: We can be flexible to Net45 for Acme given the size of the commit — I’ve looped in Karthik to confirm finance can accommodate Net45 and any exceptions for earlier payment discounts.

- Taxes/withholding: We are open to accepting tax residency certificates to waive withholding where allowed by local law. Legal will want language that places ultimate responsibility for withholding to the extent required by local law, but requires Acme to provide reasonably requested tax documentation.

I’m attaching the pricing spreadsheet with the staircase and a draft redline of the order form (see orderform-pricing-spreadsheet.xlsx and ACME_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf). Kimberly — can you propose concrete wording for the order form and an excerpt from the MSA re: taxes so we can send one redlined PDF back to Acme?

Next step: Kimberly to provide redline language today; Karthik to confirm Net45 and payment timing. If we can get that finalized by EOD Thu, I’ll prepare the final PDF and DocuSign flow.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Suggested redlines — taxes, invoice triggers, and proration language

Monica / Karthik —

Quick draft language for the order form and MSA excerpt. Please review and send back to Acme as a single redlined PDF:

1) Taxes/Withholding: "Customer shall be responsible for any taxes, duties, or governmental charges imposed on payments made under this Order Form, excluding Redwood's income taxes. In jurisdictions where local law requires Customer to withhold taxes from payments to Redwood, Customer shall deduct such withholding, pay the withheld amounts to the appropriate authority, and provide Redwood with official receipts or tax residency documentation within thirty (30) days. If Customer provides a valid certificate of residence or other applicable documentation, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to assist Customer in obtaining any applicable tax relief or exemption."

2) Payment triggers / Invoicing: "Invoices will be issued monthly in arrears based on actual usage and/or the committed units for the billing period. For changes to committed units (upsells or downsells) mid-billing period, Redwood will: (a) for upsells, prorate the additional committed units from the effective date and invoice accordingly; (b) for downsells, permit the reduced commit to take effect following a thirty (30) day notice, and issue a true-up invoice for any shortfall for prior billing periods. Any credits issued will be applied to subsequent invoices only; no cash refunds will be provided except where required by law."

3) Minimum commit true-up: "If Customer's actual usage during a calendar quarter is less than seventy percent (70%) of the committed units for that quarter, Redwood may issue a true-up invoice to reconcile the shortfall. The parties may agree in writing on alternative thresholds for specific accounts; such exceptions must be documented in the order form schedule."

4) Net terms: "Standard payment terms are Net30. For Enterprise Customers with annual committed spend exceeding USD 500,000, Net45 may be extended upon mutual written agreement. Late payments shall accrue interest at 1.5% per month or the maximum permitted by law, whichever is less."

I attached the MSA-excerpt-tax-clause.pdf with context. If Acme pushes to shift withholding liability to Redwood in all cases, we should decline — instead offer the residency-certificate route and expedited receipts for their tax filings.

Monica — if this looks good, I recommend returning a single PDF with tracked changes and a short cover email summarizing the concessions (Net45, proration for upsells, 30-day downsell notice).

Kimberly Park
Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Monica / Kimberly / Karthik —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and proposed language. A few quick clarifications from Acme Legal:

• The residency-certificate approach is acceptable, but we need Redwood to commit to providing an invoice stub that shows tax line items and a mechanism to receive receipts from local authorities if withholding occurs.

• Net45 is preferable for our AP cadence; we appreciate the offer to extend Net45 for accounts > $500k. Our expected annual commit for the first year is in that band — please confirm formally if that will apply to our order.

• For the true-up clause: Acme would prefer any true-up invoice to be limited to two consecutive quarters rather than immediate single-quarter clawbacks. Can you confirm a compromise (e.g., 70% threshold applied per quarter but capped to reconcile no more than two quarters retrospectively)?

If you can incorporate the invoice stub example and the two-quarter cap into the redline, we should be able to circulate internally and sign next week. Please return a single redlined PDF for our legal to review; a sample invoice stub in the body of the PDF would be ideal.

Best,
Jane Doe
Senior Counsel, Acme Analytics
